title: afs operations
description: The three ways to run afs and the six request operations each of them accepts. A request is a JSON object whose `op` field names the operation; as an MCP tool the operation is afs_<op> and its arguments are the same fields.

entities.name: Run one request
entities.description: `afs call [JSON|-]`: runs one request, or an array of them in order, in a fresh session and prints the reply.
entities.transport: command line: `afs call '<json>'`, or the JSON on stdin when the argument is omitted or `-`
entities.authorization: None: nothing checks who calls; afs reads whatever the user running it may read.
entities.result: One JSON reply on stdout (an array of replies for an array); exit code 0 when every reply has ok: true, else 1. No session memory: nothing is ever unchanged.
failures: Text that is not JSON: {"ok":false,"error":"invalid JSON: …"} and exit code 1.
Any reply in a batch has ok: false: exit code 1 with every reply printed.
stdin that is not UTF-8: `afs: …` on stderr and exit code 1.

entities.name: Run a JSONL session
entities.description: `afs jsonl`: one request per stdin line, one reply per stdout line, all in one session.
entities.transport: stdin and stdout of `afs jsonl`, newline-delimited JSON
entities.authorization: None: nothing checks who calls; afs reads whatever the user running it may read.
entities.result: A reply line per non-blank request line until stdin closes; repeats within the session get unchanged markers and diffs.
failures: A line that is not JSON: an {"ok":false,"error":"invalid JSON: …"} line, and the loop goes on.
Input that is not UTF-8: the loop stops with `afs: …` on stderr and exit code 1.

entities.name: Serve MCP over stdio
entities.description: `afs serve`: a Model Context Protocol server on stdin and stdout with one session per process.
entities.transport: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 on stdio: initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call; messages without an id are notifications and get no reply
entities.authorization: None: nothing checks who calls; afs reads whatever the user running it may read.
entities.result: initialize returns serverInfo afs, the tools capability and usage instructions; tools/list returns afs_read, afs_search, afs_list, afs_stat, afs_outline and afs_diff_since with their input schemas; tools/call returns the operation's reply as one text content item, with isError when the reply is not ok.
failures: A line that is not JSON: JSON-RPC error -32700 with a null id.
An unknown method: JSON-RPC error -32601 `method not found`.
A tool name without the afs_ prefix: isError with `unknown tool …`.
A failed operation: isError with the operation's error reply as text.
Input that is not UTF-8: the server stops with exit code 1.

entities.name: read
entities.description: Reads a file, whole or by 1-based line ranges, capped, and remembers what this session received.
entities.authorization: None: any path the user running afs may read.
entities.result: path, etag, total_lines, chunks of {start, end, text} and ref; truncated, next_ranges and bytes_omitted when a cap (max_lines 400, max_bytes 16384 by default) stopped it; long_lines_cut when lines over 2000 bytes were cut. A repeat this session already received gives {etag, unchanged: true, ref}; if_none_match equal to the etag gives unchanged without ref; a whole-file re-read of a file whose earlier full version is still held gives changed, base_etag and hunks when they are smaller than half the file; a file with a NUL in its first 8000 bytes gives binary: true and its size.
failures: The path cannot be read: `<path>: <OS error>`.
The path is not a regular file: `<path>: not a regular file (use list for directories)`.
A range starting at 0 or ending before it starts: `bad range [s,e]: lines are 1-based and start must be <= end`.
An unknown field: the parser's error.

entities.name: search
entities.description: Regex or literal search over files under the given paths, honouring ignore files, grouped by file and cached.
entities.authorization: None: any path the user running afs may read.
entities.result: results (per file: hits rendered with the chosen fields, or blocks of merged context lines), files_matched, total_matches, and etag, cached and ref; files instead of results with files_only; truncated when max_matches (100 by default) cut it. A repeat already received gives {etag, unchanged: true, ref}.
failures: A pattern that does not compile: `bad pattern: …`.
A field other than path, line, col or text: `unknown field …; use path, line, col, text`; no field left after path: `fields must include line, col or text`.
A path that does not exist: `<path>: no such file or directory`.
A malformed glob: `glob <glob>: …`.

entities.name: list
entities.description: Lists a directory, one level unless a glob or depth is given, honouring ignore files, sorted and paged.
entities.authorization: None: any path the user running afs may read.
entities.result: entries (path strings, directories with a trailing slash; [path, size, mtime] with long), total, etag, cached and ref; truncated and next_cursor when max_entries (500 by default) cut it. With a glob, only matching files are listed, at any depth unless depth is given.
failures: A path that does not exist: `<path>: no such file or directory`.
A malformed glob: `glob <glob>: …`.

entities.name: stat
entities.description: Metadata of one path, without following symlinks, and optionally its content etag.
entities.authorization: None: any path the user running afs may read.
entities.result: exists: false for a missing path; otherwise kind (file, dir, symlink or other), size and mtime, plus etag for a regular file when hash is true. Not cached and never unchanged.
failures: hash: true on a regular file that cannot be read: `<path>: <OS error>`.

entities.name: outline
entities.description: Symbols with their line ranges for every supported source file under the paths.
entities.authorization: None: any path the user running afs may read.
entities.result: files of {path, symbols: [[start, end, kind, name], …]} sorted by path, total_symbols, etag, cached and ref; truncated when max_symbols (300 by default) cut it. Files without symbols, unsupported, binary or unreadable files are left out.
failures: A path that does not exist: `<path>: no such file or directory`.

entities.name: diff_since
entities.description: Line hunks between a version of a file this session still holds, named by its etag, and the file now.
entities.authorization: None: any path the user running afs may read.
entities.result: path, base_etag, etag, newlines (the count of newline bytes), hunks of {at, del, new_at, ins} and ref; {etag, unchanged: true} when the file still has that etag.
failures: The etag is not among the versions the session holds: `base_unavailable: that version is not held; use read`.
Either version is not UTF-8: `cannot diff non-UTF-8 content; use read`.
The file cannot be read: `<path>: <OS error>`.
